title: Pseudo-coherent algebraic effectivity of normalized finite reductions
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $J\subset C$ an ideal, and assume $C\simeq\varprojlim C/J^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Suppose $E_n\in D(C/J^n)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] are supplied with transition maps in $D(C/J^{n+1})$ inducing isomorphisms $E_{n+1}\otimes^L_{C/J^{n+1}}C/J^n\simeq E_n$. Assume $E_1$ is bounded above with finitely generated cohomology in every degree. Then $E=R\varprojlim E_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit] is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and its projections induce isomorphisms $E\otimes_C^L C/J^n\simeq E_n$, compatible with the supplied transitions and quotient cocycles. It is derived $J$-complete, meaning $E\simeq R\varprojlim_n(E\otimes_C^L C/J^n)$. No perfectness of $E_1$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09AV, lemma-Rlim-pseudo-coherent-gives-complete-pseudo-coherent; Tag 066E, lemma-Noetherian-pseudo-coherent replaces the pseudo-coherence hypothesis by its Noetherian cohomology criterion

proof.text: The quotient C/J is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] to the given upper cohomology bound and finite cohomology, obtaining pseudo-coherence of the first level.

Use [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] to prove the compatible-tuple universal property of C as the inverse limit of C/J^(n+1). Choose representatives of a compatible tuple; compatibility makes them an adic Cauchy sequence. Precompleteness gives a limiting element and separatedness makes it unique. Every successive quotient is surjective. Its kernel is the image of J^(n+1); its square is the image of J^(2n+2), hence zero modulo J^(n+2).

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-scalar-adjunction] to obtain left adjoints to derived restriction along the successive quotient maps and the maps C to C/J^(n+1). Under an adjunction, the normalization bijections are precisely precomposition by the transpose of t_n; Yoneda makes that transpose invertible.

The exact derived composition isomorphism for scalar restriction is normalized on complexes by composing mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac and mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac. The comparison of the termwise composition functors is the identity. Thus this is precisely the restriction-composition isomorphism prescribed by the given f_n; rewriting with h_f gives the Roos triangle required for reconstruction.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pseudocoherent-inverse-ring-reconstruction] to these quotient rings, their compatible-tuple limit C, the adjunctions, normalized transitions and specified Roos triangle. Its first two conclusions give pseudo-coherence of E and invertibility of every transpose of its projection. Run it once with chosen left adjoints to obtain pseudo-coherence, and with each supplied family of left adjoints to obtain the claimed comparison maps.

For every supplied adjunction, form the isomorphism whose hom is the projection transpose. The adjunction triangle identity identifies its restriction after the unit with the original projection. In a Roos triangle the first and second arrows compose to zero, so the projections commute with consecutive transitions. NatTrans.ofOpSequence then gives their compatibility for every ordered pair of levels. Componentwise restriction of the comparison isomorphisms identifies the two products. Its product map conjugates the shift operators and hence 1 minus those operators. The identity on E and this product isomorphism identify the Roos triangles, proving that E is a derived limit of its reductions [def-weil-derived-limit].

lean.note: Positive level n+1 is indexed by n. Normalization is expanded as the universal property of derived scalar extension against exact derived restriction. For every choice of derived scalar-extension adjunctions, the conclusion identifies their comparison maps with the adjuncts of the specified Roos projections and states derived completeness for the transported reduction tower. No additional flatness, perfectness or boundedness hypothesis is imposed.
